crm_notes: CTO (Dr. Elena Morales): must not send raw PHI to third-party without BAAs and encryption-at-rest with customer KMS.
Priority: replace slow EHR search (avg 900ms, 75th pct 1.4s) with sub-300ms median for clinician workflows.

Customer wants hybrid approach: dense embeddings for semantic recall + reranker for clinical precision (safety-first).
Cost sensitivity: operating budget constraint for hosted tokens; prefer Dedicated or Private to control unit cost at scale.
SE notes: recommended quantized embedding models + sharded ANN store; suggested caching top-K prefixes for hot patient records.
Legal: legal team insists on audit trail for every query (user id, patient id hash, timestamp) and 7-year log retention for certain cohorts.
Quote from Chief Data Officer: 'If we can't prove deterministic logging and key custody on day one, we cannot proceed to pilot.'
Closed-loop request: include eval harness to measure clinical-fidelity (precision@k by case mix) and worst-case latency SLOs.

technical_requirements: Median query latency target: <= 250ms for single-shot RAG (embed+ANN+rerkank) in US-East region
Throughput: baseline 60 qps for outpatient portal; burst capacity to 300 qps during daily batch uploads
Indexing: support incremental upserts and soft-deletes at 2M docs/day; cold-storage for older cohorts
Retrieval architecture: vector store with configurable ANN algorithm (HNSW / IVF) and deterministic reranker stage
KV cache for patient context (prefix caching) and strict KV eviction policies tied to PHI retention rules
Key management: bring-your-own KMS (AES-256) with HSM-backed key wrapping
Network: VPC peering or private link; no public internet egress for PHI in production
